# Weekend, session S1 — wafer-tool-shift

*Regenerated by `scripts/weekend.py`; numbers computed from `runs/` at write time. HEAD: `e606cf0 Answer the handed-down target with numbers instead of caveats`. Long form in `critique_log.md` and `paper_draft.md`.*

## The short version

Three claims this repo made on Friday are now withdrawn, all of them because of controls that had never been run. Nothing was withdrawn because of a new idea beating an old one; the weekend's output is almost entirely negative results, and they are the useful kind — each one closes off a direction that looked open.

## 1. Headline numbers, Friday against now

| protocol | representation | Friday (1 seed) | now | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lot` | rpca_cnn | 0.8813 | 0.8696 ±0.0096 (n=3) | **Friday reported the top of this range** |
| `lot` | cnn_gn | 0.8671 | 0.8647 ±0.0044 (n=3) | Friday reported one seed from inside this range |
| `lot` | cnn_bn | 0.8587 | 0.8522 ±0.0069 (n=3) | **Friday reported the top of this range** |
| `lot` | spectral | 0.8538 | 0.8538 (n=1) |  |
| `lot` | feat | 0.8417 | 0.8417 (n=1) |  |
| `lot_time` | cnn_gn | 0.6935 | 0.6985 ±0.0045 (n=3) | Friday reported the bottom of this range |
| `size` | cnn_gn | 0.8203 | 0.8467 ±0.0346 (n=3) | Friday reported the bottom of this range |

**Nothing here got better, and that is the point.** The numbers moved because they acquired seeds, not because the models changed. Friday's table reported 59 cells at one seed each and no measurement of what a seed is worth.

## 2. What was tried, what failed, and what that rules out

### 2.1 The RPCA lot-signature channel — withdrawn

| protocol | fourth channel | macro-F1 | vs no channel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lot` | RPCA residual (the claim) | 0.8696 ±0.0096 (n=3) | +0.0049 |
| `lot` | raw failed-die mask | 0.8692 ±0.0065 (n=3) | +0.0045 |
| `lot` | **zeros** | 0.8689 ±0.0075 (n=3) | +0.0042 |
| `lot` | no fourth channel | 0.8647 ±0.0044 (n=3) | — |
| `lot_time` | RPCA residual (the claim) | 0.7088 ±0.0070 (n=3) | +0.0103 |
| `lot_time` | raw failed-die mask | 0.7004 ±0.0096 (n=3) | +0.0019 |
| `lot_time` | **zeros** | 0.7018 ±0.0030 (n=3) | +0.0033 |
| `lot_time` | no fourth channel | 0.6985 ±0.0045 (n=3) | — |
| `size` | RPCA residual (the claim) | 0.8421 ±0.0359 (n=3) | -0.0046 |
| `size` | raw failed-die mask | 0.8421 ±0.0343 (n=3) | -0.0045 |
| `size` | **zeros** | 0.8398 ±0.0312 (n=3) | -0.0069 |
| `size` | no fourth channel | 0.8467 ±0.0346 (n=3) | — |

`rpca_cnn` was the best `lot` cell at 0.8813. The RPCA low-rank part is rank 0 for 94.83% of decomposed lots and its residual is bit-identical to the raw failed-die mask for 95.27% of all wafers, so the "lot signature channel" is mostly a second copy of a channel the input already had. On `lot`, a fourth channel of **zeros** buys the same as the decomposition. **Rules out:** per-lot RPCA as a domain normalization on this corpus. Lots here do not share enough for the decomposition to have anything to remove.

### 2.2 Lot-adversarial SSL pretraining — costs 5 to 8 points

| protocol | from scratch | SSL-initialized | difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lot` | 0.8647 ±0.0044 (n=3) | 0.8143 ±0.0091 (n=3) | -0.0504 |
| `size` | 0.8467 ±0.0346 (n=3) | 0.7711 ±0.0265 (n=3) | -0.0756 |
| `lot_time` | 0.6985 ±0.0045 (n=3) | 0.6345 ±0.0225 (n=3) | -0.0640 |

On every protocol the best SSL-initialized seed is below the worst from-scratch seed — the ranges do not overlap. These cells existed only as a `runs/` gap on Friday: `sweep_c.sh` built its log filename with `tr -d ' -'`, which left the slash in `--init-from runs/ssl_pretrain.pt`, so bash failed to open the redirect and the python process never started. Three cells were logged as launched and never ran, with no error anywhere a person would look.

**Not yet a paper claim.** Every cell fine-tunes at one LR chosen for a random init, and the pretrained weights are 5.8x larger in the deepest conv. `scripts/ssl_lr_sweep.sh` runs *both* arms at four LRs. **Rules out, if it survives:** this masked-die + gradient-reversal recipe on 638,506 unlabelled wafers.

### 2.3 The `p10 domain F1` column cannot rank models

25 separate `lot` cells report an identical p10 of 0.489796 and 11 more report exactly 0.500000. A lot holds at most 25 wafers, so a lot whose single defect is missed scores exactly (48/49 + 0)/2 = 0.4898 whichever model missed it. The metric that was supposed to stop a model hiding a bad tool behind a good average could not separate any two models. Replaced by `mean_domain_macro_f1` and `frac_domains_below_half`, which average over ~1,700 lots. **Rules out:** per-lot worst-group statistics on domains this small, for any model comparison on this corpus.

### 2.4 The domain-generalization negative result — withdrawn on `lot`, stands on `size`

Every group-aware objective received `lot % 32` as its domain: 10,762 lots averaged into 32 buckets whose mean pairwise label total-variation is **0.0208**, against 0.1666 between real lots. Equalizing 32 distributions that are already equal is something every invariance penalty achieves by doing nothing, so "no objective beats ERM on `lot`" was close to guaranteed by construction. On `size` the same hash is not degenerate (TV 0.2592) and that column's large negative effects — GroupDRO −0.18 to −0.27 — stand.

| objective | domain = `lot % 32` | domain = production decile | difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `coral` | 0.8468 ±0.0090 (n=3) | 0.8443 ±0.0098 (n=3) | -0.0025 |
| `dann` | 0.8517 ±0.0080 (n=3) | 0.8454 ±0.0132 (n=3) | -0.0062 |
| `erm` | 0.8522 ±0.0069 (n=3) | 0.8514 ±0.0073 (n=3) | -0.0008 |
| `group_dro` | 0.8535 ±0.0063 (n=3) | 0.8257 ±0.0139 (n=3) | -0.0277 |
| `hsic` | 0.8527 ±0.0080 (n=3) | 0.8488 ±0.0076 (n=3) | -0.0039 |
| `irm` | 0.8418 ±0.0094 (n=3) | 0.8465 ±0.0052 (n=3) | +0.0047 |
| `mixup_domain` | 0.8398 ±0.0108 (n=3) | 0.8371 ±0.0138 (n=3) | -0.0027 |

### 2.4b Withdrawn: "active learning lost to random"

At the 400-lot budget the published table reads random 0.7241, diverse 0.6581, coreset 0.5938, entropy 0.5698. The same JSON records how many wafers each strategy actually labelled:

| at 400 lots | wafers labelled | wafers per lot | share of random's wafers |
|---|---|---|---|
| random | 6,284 | 15.71 | 100.0% |
| entropy | 1,104 | 2.76 | 17.6% |
| coreset | 1,820 | 4.55 | 29.0% |
| diverse | 1,344 | 3.36 | 21.4% |

The heuristics were losing while training on a fifth of the data. A lot's acquisition score is the *mean* of its wafers' scores, and the maximum of noisy means favours small samples, so "take the top-scoring lots" is partly "take the smallest lots". Straight from the stored table, entropy reaches 0.7285 on 2,464 wafers, which random never reaches at any budget it was measured at. **Rules out nothing yet** — the confound is certain but the reversal rests on 3 seeds and interpolation, so the grid is being re-run with the budget in wafers.

### 2.5 The forward-only result is a compound, not pure temporal drift

| protocol | geometries in train | in test | test wafers of unseen geometry |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iid` | 327 | 266 | 0.05% |
| `lot` | 320 | 209 | 0.28% |
| `size` | 205 | 139 | 100.00% |
| `lot_time` | 338 | 19 | 14.15% |

`lot_time` tests on **19 geometries** against 338 in training, and 14.15% of its test wafers are of a geometry never trained on — against 0.28% for `lot`. The forward-only drop is therefore part temporal drift and part the `size` protocol arriving through the back door. The split between the two is not yet measured and is not guessed; `run_bench.py` now evaluates the seen- and unseen-geometry halves of every test set and the backfill is the next stage to run.

Separately, the lot numbering is **not** arbitrary: bucketing lots into deciles of lot number and correlating decile gap against distributional distance, against a null of 200 reassignments of numbers to lots, gives Spearman +0.3834 for geometry (p 0.000) and +0.4050 for failed-die rate (p 0.000). The defect-class mix does *not* drift (p 0.055). This kills the "those are just arbitrary IDs" objection but cannot separate production order from product blocking; both give this signature.

### 2.6 Run-to-run reproducibility floor

The same cell run 6 times under identical arguments spans **0.0054** in test macro-F1: 0.8723, 0.8760, 0.8767, 0.8767, 0.8772, 0.8778. Two cells closer together than that have not been shown to differ at all, whatever their arguments — and every verdict in `RESULTS.md` now requires the margin between two cells' seed ranges to exceed it.

The stored value for that cell, 0.8671, is **outside** those repeats — 0.0052 below the nearest, with every repeat above it. The code is not the cause: the pre-weekend code re-run on these GPUs lands inside the current range. The stored cells were measured on GPUs 2/3, which belong to another session and were not taken to check this. So total spread across sessions is roughly twice the within-session figure, and the seed spreads quoted elsewhere understate it because a cell's seeds are all run back-to-back on one pair of devices. `scripts/backfill_metrics.sh` refuses to overwrite measured cells while that is true.

### 2.7 Closed without a run: the label-aware split guard never fires

Both external reviewers flagged that `_stratified_group_split` reads candidate groups' labels to decide what may be held out. Dropping the guard entirely and comparing the partitions, no model involved:

| protocol | seeds where the guard fired | seeds where the split differed | seeds where label-blind lost a class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lot` | 0 / 10 | 0 / 10 | 0 / 10 |
| `size` | 0 / 10 | 0 / 10 | 0 / 10 |

The bias is not small, it is zero: the partitions are identical wafer for wafer at every seed. Structurally so — the guard rejects a group only if that group holds *all* remaining training examples of some class, and no lot holds more than 4.14% of any class. The code path is label-aware; the split is not. This was in last revision's decision list on the strength of two reviewers agreeing; four minutes of CPU would have settled it first.

### 2.8 The target, answered: 0.95 is not reachable here and focal is not the reason

| protocol | best loss | multi-label macro-F1 | vs the 0.95 target |
|---|---|---|---|
| optimistic (random source split) | `focal` | 0.8427 | -0.1073 |
| honest (lot-disjoint sources) | `focal` | 0.8177 | -0.1323 |

Measured on **MIXED-SYNTH**, which is synthetic — mixed-type wafers built by OR-ing two same-geometry WM-811K wafers — and therefore an *upper bound* on the real mixed-type task, since overlaid patterns do not interact the way compound defects do. So the closest figure to the target is the optimistic split of an easier-than-real dataset, and it still misses by more than a tenth. Focal's seed range overlaps plain BCE's on both protocols, and positive-class weighting is clearly worse: the loss named in the target contributes nothing.

## 3. Four things that need a human decision

**Decision 1 — MixedWM38, or drop the multi-label target.** The target says "multi-label F1 ≥ 0.95". WM-811K is single-label over 9 classes, so that number is not defined on it. MixedWM38 could not be acquired from this machine: the HuggingFace copy (`wafervqaanon/MixedWM38-VQA`) is gated behind manual approval and Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20061545 returns HTTP 403 on its files. Options:

  - **(a)** Give the box Kaggle credentials (`~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`) or request access to the gated HuggingFace copy, and the multi-label number becomes measurable on the real benchmark. One human action.
  - **(b)** Accept **MIXED-SYNTH** — built this weekend, overlaid WM-811K patterns, lot-disjoint, labelled synthetic in every artefact — and report it as an *upper bound*, because overlaid patterns do not interact the way real compound defects do.
  - **(c)** Drop the multi-label target as not well posed on this corpus and report 9-class macro-F1 instead, stating why.

  *Recommendation: (a) if anyone can spare five minutes for the credentials, else (b) with the upper-bound caveat kept prominent.*

**Decision 2 — what to do about the 0.95 target, now that it is measured.** Section 2.8 gives the multi-label numbers and section 1 the single-label ones; every reading misses, and the closest is the optimistic split of a synthetic upper bound. The best lot-disjoint cell is 0.8647 ±0.0044 (n=3) and the best iid cell is 0.8855 (n=1). Published figures near 0.95 are 9-class iid splits with heavy augmentation, which is the `iid` column and a different quantity. Options: **(a)** keep the lot-disjoint number as the headline and report the gap to the optimistic protocol as the contribution; **(b)** chase 0.95 on `iid` with augmentation and a bigger backbone, and report it clearly as the optimistic protocol. *Recommendation: (a). The gap is the paper; closing it by loosening the split is the one thing the rules here forbid.*

**Decision 4 — which acquisition cost model is the real one?** The active-learning comparison depends entirely on it and the two answers disagree. If a metrology slot costs one **lot** whatever its size, the published lot-budget curve is right and the finding is that these heuristics waste slots on near-empty lots. If the cost is per **wafer measured**, the wafer axis is right and the heuristics are ahead of random. Measured in a smoke run of the new code: to acquire ~780 wafers, random needed 50 lots and entropy needed 360 — same data, seven times the slots. *Recommendation: state the fab's actual cost model and report the curve for it, with the other beside it. This is the one question here that only someone who knows the metrology contract can answer.*

**Decision 3 — how should the forward-only result be framed?** It is the repo's largest number and it is a compound. `lot_time` tests on a narrow geometry slice with a seventh of its wafers of geometries never trained on (section 2.5), so "forward-only *time* costs 20 points" is not what was measured. Options: **(a)** reframe it as *forward-only deployment* — you meet new products and new tools going forward, and the geometry shift is part of the phenomenon, not a confound to remove; **(b)** build a geometry-controlled temporal protocol that holds the geometry mix fixed across the time boundary, isolating drift but measuring something a fab never actually experiences; **(c)** report both. *Recommendation: (a) as the headline with the decomposition printed beside it. A fab does not get to hold its product mix fixed, so (b) measures a cleaner quantity that matters less. The decomposition that makes (a) honest is queued and is the next stage to land.*

## 4. What is still running, and how to check it

Stages run one at a time on GPUs 0 and 1: `scripts/chain_s1.sh` then `scripts/chain_rest.sh`, which waits on a marker line in the previous stage's log. Nothing runs in parallel with anything else, so a stage that hangs stops the queue rather than oversubscribing the two leased devices.

```
tail -f logs/chain_s1.log      # which stage is up
nvidia-smi                     # devices 0,1 only; 2,3 belong to another loop
ls -t runs/*.json | head       # newest cells
python scripts/report.py && python scripts/paper.py && python scripts/weekend.py
python tests/run_tests.py      # no pytest in the pdeno env, by design
```

| stage | status | log | what it decides |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sinkhorn_lambda.sh` | done | `logs/sinkhorn_lambda.log` | 7 OT weights incl. 0 as an ERM control through the same wrapper, with the penalty itself logged. **Answered**: tuned on validation it is +0.0004 over ERM and the penalty is never reduced -- inert, not a tradeoff |
| `domain_def_sweep.sh` | done | `logs/domain_def.log` | 7 objectives x {lot%32, production decile} x 3 seeds. The headline re-test: does the DG negative result survive a domain definition that carries real shift? |
| `backfill_metrics.sh` | running | `logs/backfill.log` | the seen/unseen-geometry decomposition on every ERM cell -- how much of the forward-only drop is geometry rather than time -- plus the metrics added since these cells ran. Measures the run-to-run floor first and **refuses to overwrite** anything if stored values do not reproduce within it |
| `mixed_sweep.sh` | done | `logs/mixed_sweep.log` | MIXED-SYNTH, 3 losses incl. focal, both protocols, 2 seeds |
| `ssl_lr_sweep.sh` | done | `logs/ssl_lr.log` | both arms at 3 more LRs; the confound check on the -5 to -8 point SSL result |
| `longtail_sweep.sh` | done | `logs/longtail.log` | focal gamma over {0, 0.5, 1, 2, 5} plus class weighting, 2 seeds; gamma=0 is bit-exact ERM and is the built-in control |

Nothing writes outside this repository, nothing touches GPUs 2 or 3, and no package was installed into any shared environment. `runs.bak_*/` is a copy of `runs/` as it stood on Friday, gitignored, kept so any re-run can be checked against what it replaced.
